title: The IPC confirms famine in Gaza Governorate, the first declared in the Middle East
body:
On Friday 22 August 2025, the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), a UN-backed global hunger monitor, confirmed famine with reasonable evidence in Gaza Governorate, which covers Gaza City and about 20 percent of the Strip. AFP reported it was the first famine declared in the Middle East. The analysis covered data from 1 July to 15 August 2025 and projected that famine would spread to Deir el-Balah and Khan Yunis governorates by the end of September, covering about two-thirds of the territory.

The IPC said more than 500,000 people faced catastrophic conditions, a figure it expected to rise to nearly 641,000, about a third of the population, by the end of September. About 98 percent of Gaza's cropland was damaged, inaccessible or both. The IPC cited a sharp escalation of the war, mass displacement and severe restrictions on food and commercial supplies, noting that Israel banned aid in early March and allowed only very limited quantities from late May. A famine declaration requires that at least 20 percent of households face extreme food shortages, at least 30 percent of children under five are acutely malnourished, and at least two in 10,000 people die daily.

UN aid chief Tom Fletcher said the famine was preventable and blamed systematic obstruction by Israel for food stacking up at borders. Israel's foreign ministry said there was no famine in Gaza and rejected the report as based on Hamas lies laundered through organisations with vested interests. AFP cited the Gaza Health Ministry's figure of at least 62,192 Palestinians killed in the war, which the UN considers reliable.
